direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: View with two cards in the corner
hero.blueprint: One photograph or muted film fills the viewport, `object-fit: cover`, with the subject in the right half. The headline sits on the left at mid-height: two lines at clamp(44px, 3.9vw, 60px), bold, leading 1.08, flush to the 32px margin on columns 1–5, the block vertically centred; 20px below it, one supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, in the paper colour. In the bottom-right corner, 32px from the right and bottom edges, two cards sit side by side with a 16px gap, each two columns wide (about 210px) at 3:2: a photograph of the newest thing (a project, an edition, an article) with a paper-colour bar 40px tall fused to its lower edge, holding its title at 16px on the left and a small arrow on the right. They are the next steps after the single action, which is a solid rectangle top-right beside a menu word. One short fact at 16px in the paper colour may be pinned onto the subject itself, beside a solid 8px dot on the point it describes, with no line joining them. Wordmark top-left on the 32px margin. If the left half is light, lay a neutral dark scrim under columns 1–6 only.
hero.mobile: The picture is re-cropped to portrait with the subject in the upper half. The headline sits at 9vw on two lines on the 16px margin at 44% of the height, with the sentence at 16px beneath it. The two cards sit side by side across the full width at the bottom, 16px from the edges, each about 171px wide at 3:2 with its title bar. Wordmark top-left; the action and a menu word top-right.
hero.headline: A plain two-line claim of 4–7 words, at most about 17 characters per line at 3.9vw.

type.note: A narrow, sharp display serif for headlines against a small plain sans: a five-to-one jump with nothing between. Suits agencies, bakeries and restaurants, fashion and editorial brands.

palette.name: Cobalt on sand
palette.note: Sand paper and one cobalt do everything: text, drawings and solid shapes are all the same blue. The button is a cobalt block with sand-coloured type, and no black or second hue is used.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Headline crossing onto a photograph
sections.blueprint: A white or pale ground. A photograph taller than it is wide, 720px wide (columns 7–12), sits flush against the right viewport edge with its top at 46% of the section's first screen and runs below the fold. The heading starts on the 32px left margin across columns 1–8: two lines of light-weight serif capitals at clamp(64px, 5.6vw, 88px), leading 1.04, the first line starting 34% down the screen and the second placed so that its right half runs onto the photograph's upper-left corner. Choose a picture whose upper-left quarter is pale enough for the ink, or set the second line twice, in the ink and in the paper colour, each copy clipped to its side of the photograph's left edge. Under the heading on columns 1–5, one paragraph of up to 25 words at 22px, leading 1.4. At the bottom-left a second, smaller photograph of 360×400px enters, cropped by the screen's lower edge, and on the next screen becomes the left half of a staggered pair with the large one. Nothing else is on the screen.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines on the 20px margin. The photograph becomes 75% of the width, flush right, and starts under the heading's first line so the second line crosses its top-left corner. The paragraph follows at 17px, then the small photograph at 50% of the width on the left margin.

sections.name: Fixed output, live controls
sections.blueprint: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
sections.mobile: The output sits in a sticky field at the top, 42svh tall, cropped to its most telling region, not shrunk. Blocks scroll beneath on the page ground: sentence at 22px, paragraph at 16px, control at full width with 44px targets. The field releases after the last block.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Recognition as a table
sections.blueprint: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
sections.mobile: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

sections.name: The idea again, inverted
sections.blueprint: The close flips the page's colours: ink becomes the ground and the ground becomes the ink, across a full-bleed field at least 90svh tall. The page's opening idea returns as a headline of three to five words at 9–11vw on two lines, leading 0.9, flush left, positioned in the upper two-thirds; it should echo the hero's wording, not repeat it. Along the bottom, on one shared baseline 40px above the edge: one supporting sentence at 20px in columns 1–5 and one rectangular button in the accent colour, right-aligned in columns 10–12, about 56px tall. Nothing else: no image, no second button, no logo. The field's top edge is a hard horizontal line where it meets the section above. If the footer follows on the same inverted field, leave 160px before it so the close still reads as its own screen.
sections.mobile: The same inverted field at 80svh. Headline at 15vw on two lines at the top. The sentence sits lower at 17px, and the button spans the full width at the bottom, 56px tall, with 20px margins. Nothing else is added.

references.name: Architecture of Socialist-Era Belgrade
references.idea: A two-colour printed guidebook on screen: signal-red type over greyscale concrete, with one modular display face as the only ornament.
references.hero: Full-bleed greyscale photograph of brutalist housing towers; pale sky fills the top half, concrete the bottom. The title is set over the sky, flush left at a 32px margin, three lines in a wide modular display face at 102px (7.1vw) in flat red, the longest line reaching 92% of the width, leading so tight that the lines almost touch. Under it, one row at 24px: a red one-line descriptor at left, and two paler-red facts right-aligned (an object count and a date range). Top-right, the word 'Index' with a diagonal arrow. No logo, no button, nothing else. Red and grey only.
references.type: IntraNet, a wide modular display face with rounded, notched corners, used only for the title and its footer repeat. Funnel Sans carries the rest: about 50px for the long intro, 40px bold uppercase entry titles, 24px meta, 13px credits. Four sizes, two faces.
references.colour: #f53843 #d1d1d1 #c7c7c7 #777777 #f1a7ab — Strictly red and grey: red text on grey photo or grey paper, then pale grey text on a solid red field for the essay and footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair.
references.imagery: Contemporary black-and-white architectural photographs of concrete towers and complexes, frontal or looking up, with big skies and visible grain; full-bleed in the hero, full column width and square-cornered in entries.
references.layout: 16 to 32px margins, everything flush left. A long red essay block in very large text, then twenty repeated entry blocks on grey: a two-column header split by a vertical red hairline, a meta row, then a wide photo. 81 screens of the same rhythm.

sections.description: Immediately under the hero photo a solid red field begins with no gap. The essay runs as one full-width column in pale grey sans at roughly 50px with tight leading, about 50 characters per line, paragraphs separated by one blank line, with no headings, pull-quotes or images for several screens. The photo's bottom edge butts straight against the red.

Each building entry sits on light grey paper: a thin red rule across the top, then two columns divided by a vertical red hairline at the 50% mark. Left: the building's name in red bold uppercase at 40px over two lines. Right: its dates in pale red at the same size. Below, a small meta row with 'Credits' and 'Address' labels and values in 13px red, then a full-width greyscale photograph.

Solid red. At the top, two short 13px notes side by side in pale grey occupy the left 60%, a back-to-top link sits far right, and a third note runs beneath. A tall empty red gap follows. Then the full title is repeated in the display face at hero size but in pale grey, flush left, above a single row of small meta: sources link left, font credits centre, city and year right.

steal: Limit the page to one saturated colour and one grey, desaturate all photos, and invert the pair (grey on red) for long reading blocks.
Set the title in a distinctive modular display face directly on the sky area of a photo and repeat it in the footer in the inverse colour.
Put facts in the hero as a right-aligned row of paler-tint figures (count, date range) on the same baseline as the subtitle.

references.name: Applied Imagination
references.idea: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.
references.hero: A pale blue sky fading to warm cream fills the viewport, with white clouds shaded in halftone dots. A tiny serif logotype sits top-centre; no nav. The title, two centred lines of black wedge-serif at 8.9vw, occupies the middle half of the screen and about 73% of its width; a cloud layer passes in front of the second line's baseline so the feet of the letters dissolve into dots. A two-line centred deck at 24px sits beneath. A mono byline strip is centred on the bottom edge with a scroll cue bottom-right. On the left edge at mid-height, a short vertical rule carries a two-line mono altitude readout.
references.type: fsKim, a sturdy wedge-serif display face, regular weight at 128px with -0.01em tracking for the title and pull quotes; gtAmerica at 24px for the deck and about 16px for essay body; gtAmericaMono uppercase around 11px with wide tracking for byline, altitude and tape labels.
references.colour: #cbe4f2 #f1e3b5 #0a0a0a #ffc013 #8e2f8f #f04e23 — Sky blue melting into sand yellow is the constant ground and text is black. Saturated magenta, orange and yellow arrive only in collage objects, tape labels and the footer contact card.
references.imagery: Photo-collage cut-outs (parachutes carrying a treasure chest and a burning dumpster, a pair of legs, mountains) given a coarse halftone dot screen, layered in front of and behind the type against painted clouds.
references.layout: A narrow text column about 38% wide for essay passages, interrupted by full-width display pull quotes and collage objects floating at the edges. One continuous sky instead of sections, with a fixed left-edge altimeter. Nearly 23 screens, ending on a ground-level landscape.

sections.description: Sky background, no container. A three-line pull quote in black wedge-serif at about 7vw is centred and tightly leaded. Two cut-out parachutes hang over it: a magenta one from the top-left carrying a chest spilling coins, an orange one at lower right carrying a burning dumpster, each overlapping letterforms. Small mono labels on tilted strips of coloured tape are stuck to the objects. Words in the quote turn from grey to black as they are reached.

Running essay text in about 16px grotesk, black, in a single column roughly 38% of the viewport wide, positioned left of centre with large sky margins on both sides. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line; serif sub-statements at about 28px introduce passages. The next display quote is seen rising from below, its letters partly hidden behind cloud and blurred.

Ground level: halftone-screened mountains in green and brown rise from both sides, and the title returns at huge scale, cropped by the top edge and tucked behind the peaks. Centred below is a square-cornered two-panel card: a cream left panel with a short form of two fields and a small orange button, and a magenta right panel with a round portrait, name and a yellow subscribe button. Yellow tape-strip credits sit on the bottom edge.

steal: Tie a persistent numeric readout to scroll position (altitude falling to zero) so the reader's progress becomes part of the story.
Layer an illustration element in front of the bottom of a giant title so the letters sink into the scene instead of sitting on top.
Apply one coarse halftone dot screen to every photo cut-out so collage pieces from different sources read as one illustration set.

references.name: Sharplink
references.idea: A crypto treasury presented as precision hardware: chrome machined parts and glass capsules rendered in 3D on deep blue, overlaid with dashed machine-vision tracking boxes.
references.hero: Full-bleed video of exploded brushed-metal components floating on a navy-to-cobalt gradient, covered by a web of thin white dashed lines and small square tracking markers. Logo top-left on a 2% margin; top-right a segmented strip of five dark rectangular tabs in narrow uppercase plus an arrow square. The headline is top-left, two lines at 6.1vw in regular weight with -0.03em tracking, starting 18% down. Under it two stacked rectangular buttons: white with a blue arrow square attached, then a translucent dark one. Bottom row: a stock-exchange badge at left, a three-line lead paragraph at about 1.3vw starting 26% across, and bottom-right a translucent dark news card about 30% wide.
references.type: Archivo regular for headlines (88px in the hero, about 3vw in sections) and 16px body; Archivo Narrow in bold uppercase with wide tracking for nav, buttons and tiny labels. Headlines never go bold: hierarchy comes from size and from fading inactive items to grey.
references.colour: #050c17 #0e3f97 #e6edf7 #a7a8ab #1f6bff #ffffff — One blue family from near-black navy through cobalt to icy white; sections are vertical blue gradients, light or dark. Bright blue appears only as tiny square markers and arrow buttons; chrome grey from the renders.
references.imagery: Chrome and glass 3D objects (exploded device parts, a spike-tipped capsule holding icons) lit coolly, often with dashed annotation lines or shown as dotted wireframes; full-bleed in the hero, floating free at the right in later sections.
references.layout: 2% margins and square corners everywhere. Sections are full-viewport gradient fields with a headline at left and a 3D object or data card at right; lists run as label, title and paragraph in two columns. Tiny blue square bullets mark section starts.

sections.description: Light icy-gradient section. A two-line headline in grey-blue at about 3vw at the left, with a small paragraph far below it at bottom-left. Centre: a tall 3:4 card with a navy-to-cobalt vertical gradient, a tiny uppercase label, a rising line chart over a faint dotted grid, and a full-width dark button at its base. Right third: three faint, nearly transparent rows, each with a small numbered tag, one line of text and a ghosted line drawing.

Pinned list beside a 3D object. Left 60%: stacked rows, each with a tiny uppercase label, a two-line title at about 1.3vw in a first column and a short paragraph in a second column starting 26% across. Only the active row is at full contrast; the rest are dimmed to roughly 40%. Right 40%: a chrome-and-glass capsule about 80% of the viewport tall whose interior icon changes per row. The ground shifts from icy white to deep cobalt partway through.

A black panel inset by 2% on a navy ground with small blue square markers at its corners. Logo mark top-left; a two-line statement at about 2vw at the left, first line white and second line grey; two rectangular buttons below. A dotted wireframe version of the capsule fills the right half. Under the panel, a tiny uppercase label at left and a small button at right.

Cobalt gradient footer: a newsletter line with an underlined email field at left, three small link columns across the middle and right, exchange badge and legal microtext below. The wordmark closes the page in letters spanning the full width, cropped by the bottom edge and fading from white at the top to transparent.

steal: Overlay a 3D render with thin dashed lines and tiny square markers linking its parts, as if a vision system were tracking the object.
Build buttons as square-cornered rectangles with a separate coloured arrow square attached to the right edge.
In a pinned list beside a 3D object, dim every row except the active one and change what sits inside the object for each row.
references.media: A full-bleed 12s loop of 3D chrome and glass objects covers the whole fold, with text docked in the four corners straight on it. Below: a 3D capsule pinned in the right third while a list of claims scrolls on the left, its inner emblem swapping per row, a dark card sliding over it that turns the covered part into a dashed wireframe, a sticky portrait video of chrome pipes at the right edge, and a full-width wordmark canvas cropped by the bottom of the viewport; square corners throughout.
references.motion: The hero is composed at 400ms with the video playing and no preloader (load 21.3s), and Lenis runs four pins over fixed layers: one fixed gradient layer behind everything crossfades the grounds, the capsule stays pinned across three sections as each claim brightens from about 40% to full, and the manifesto fills character by character (423 split characters). The workhorse ease is cubic-bezier(.455,.03,.515,.955), on 57 observed opacity, background and colour transitions at .25-.3s.
